The EIN and entity name are needed for the business registration, bank account, lease and every other permit.

outcomes.original: Filing step: Register the business with the SF Treasurer & Tax Collector and file a Fictitious Business Name statement with the County Clerk. What to say: Register online at sftreasurer.org/business to obtain a Business Account Number (BAN); the fee is tiered by gross receipts (e.g., $55 up to $100k, $625 at $1–1.5M for 2026–27). The BAN is required by every city department. Then file a Fictitious Business Name (DBA) statement with the SF County Clerk in person or by mail ($60–$120), publish it once a week for four weeks in a court-approved newspaper, and file proof of publication within 45 days. Banks and ABC need the filed FBN statement.

outcomes.original: Filing step: File a Conditional Use Authorization application with SF Planning for the Restaurant use under Planning Code § 303. What to say: Submit the CUA application through the Planning Department's online portal or in person at 49 South Van Ness. The filing fee is approximately $3,150 (2026–27 CPI-adjusted rate for a no-construction CUA; fees rise with construction cost). Attach a detailed project description stating the square footage, occupant load, hours of operation, menu and food service model (Bona Fide Eating Place with table service), floor plans, a description of soundproofing and odor control measures, and a neighborhood outreach plan. State that the restaurant will comply with § 202.2(a) operating conditions and § 249.60(d) facade and lighting requirements. Planning will schedule a pre-application meeting, route the application to Police and other departments, post a 300-foot mailed notice and schedule a Planning Commission hearing. Budget 5–7 months from filing to hearing.
outcomes.note: The cited records do not contain the procedural requirements, filing fees, code section references, or application details stated in the step.

outcomes.original: Filing step: File DPH plan check for the new restaurant kitchen and finishes while the CUA is pending. What to say: Submit two sets of scaled drawings, interior/exterior photos, a detailed menu and equipment list through the DPH Environmental Health online portal at sfdph.org/dph/EH. The plan check fee is $2,207 (8 hours at $276/hour for a new restaurant, FY 2026–27). DPH reviews the layout, finishes, hand sinks, three-compartment sinks, equipment spacing, ventilation hood and grease interceptor. DPH will refer the application to Planning for zoning sign-off; Planning will hold it until the CUA is approved. Schedule a pre-final inspection at ~80% construction complete and a final inspection at least two weeks in advance, both with your assigned plan reviewer.

outcomes.original: Filing step: File a building permit application with DBI for tenant improvements and change of use, stamped by a licensed architect. What to say: Hire an architect with San Francisco restaurant experience to prepare a full plan set showing the kitchen layout, hood and fire suppression, plumbing, electrical, ADA upgrades, finishes and occupant load calculation. Submit the building permit application online at sf.gov/dbiweb or in person at 49 South Van Ness; DBI will route it to Planning, DPH, Fire, Public Works and other departments. The building permit fee is a percentage of construction valuation ($800–$15,000 depending on scope); electrical, plumbing and mechanical permits are pulled separately by licensed subcontractors. DBI will not issue the permit until Planning confirms the CUA is approved and the project conforms to the Planning Code. File this step in parallel with the CUA and DPH plan check to save time.

outcomes.original: Filing step: Apply for the ABC Type 41 licence after the CUA is approved and the building permit is issued or imminent. What to say: Submit the ABC licence application online at abc.ca.gov or by mail to the San Francisco ABC district office. Attach a copy of the approved CUA, the seller's permit, the lease, the entity documents, a diagram of the premises showing the area where alcohol will be served, and the $1,000–$1,600 application fee. Post the required ABC notice at the premises for 30 days. ABC will refer the application to SF Planning and the Police Department; Planning will confirm that the CUA covers alcohol service and that the restaurant meets Bona Fide Eating Place standards. If the census tract is over-concentrated (it is: 22 active vs. 10 authorised), ABC may require a Public Convenience or Necessity (PCN) finding from Planning or the Board of Supervisors, which can add 1–3 months. Budget 60–120 days if unprotested, longer if a PCN is required or if neighbors protest.

outcomes.original: Filing step: Complete construction, pass all final inspections (DBI, Fire, DPH) and obtain the Health Permit to Operate. What to say: Before opening, schedule and pass the final building inspection, the Fire Department hood and occupancy inspection (if occupant load ≥ 50), the SFPUC FOG grease interceptor inspection, and the DPH pre-opening inspection. DPH issues the Health Permit to Operate ($470 application fee, includes initial inspection; $0 annual licence fee for 2026–28) after confirming the facility matches the approved plans, a certified food safety manager is on staff, and all equipment and finishes are code-compliant. Do not serve food to the public before the permit is issued. Apply for ASCAP and BMI music licences ($300–$2,500 each per year) if playing recorded music or live covers. Set up organics/composting collection with the hauler (SB 1383 compliance).

outcomes.original: Estimated time: 120 to 300 days. Estimated government cost: $6,800 to $23,000. Notes: The timeline and cost are for the entitlement path approvals when they are granted: Conditional Use Authorization, Health Permit to Operate, and Building Permit with change of use. The 120–300 day range is the time to approval and reflects the CUA as the critical path (5–7 months filing to hearing, typically approved 2–4 weeks after the hearing once the motion is drafted), plus overlapping plan check and building permit review. The building permit is issued after the CUA is approved, and DPH issues the health permit after the final inspection passes. Construction time is not included. The $6,800–$23,000 cost range includes the CUA filing fee (~$3,150), DPH plan check ($2,207), DPH permit to operate ($470), building permit fees ($800–$15,000 depending on construction valuation), Fire place-of-assembly permit if occupant load ≥ 50 ($446–$1,500), and FOG interceptor registration ($0–$500). It does not include construction costs, the ABC Type 41 licence ($1,000–$1,600, state agency, not on the entitlement path because how the licence will be obtained is not known), state and federal registrations ($70–$150 entity formation, $0 EIN and seller's permit), business registration ($55–$700), sign permit ($300–$1,500), music licences (~$600–$5,000/year combined), or professional fees (architect, contractor, expediter). The CUA fee may qualify for a First Year Free waiver if this is a new storefront business in a Priority Equity Geography; confirm eligibility with Planning. ABC review runs in parallel but is not included in the city entitlement path because the alcohol row status is insufficient information.
